title: AI key
description: Read result screenshots on your own AI account.
lockNotice: Only the organization's owner or a member who manages the organization can connect or change its AI key.
what1: OCR reads the standings off a Free Fire result screen for you, so nobody types 48 rows by hand.
what2: When a screenshot needs the AI engine, it runs on your own key and your provider bills you: well under one cent per screenshot.
what3: AFC pays for one such read per organization, so you can see how it works. After that, connect your key here to keep using OCR.
what4: AFC never sees your bill and cannot read your key back once it is saved.
freeReadsLeft: {count, plural, one {You still have # free read.} other {You still have # free reads.}}
freeReadsGone: Your free read has been used. Connect a key to keep using OCR.
ocrDisabledByAdmin: OCR has been switched off for this organization by AFC. Contact support.
confirmDisconnect: Disconnect this key? OCR reads will stop until another key is connected (or a free read is left).
costLine: about ${usd} per screenshot on the recommended model, checked on {date}. Check the provider's own page for today's price.
wrong1: "Incorrect API key" or "invalid x-api-key": the key was copied with a space, or a character is missing. Paste it again.
wrong2: "Insufficient quota", "credit balance too low" or "exceeded your current quota": your provider account has no credit. Top it up on the provider's page and test again.
wrong3: "Model not found": the model id is wrong for this provider. Put the recommended one back.
reportStep: A step looks wrong? Providers rename buttons.
reportStepLink: Tell us and we fix the line.
modelHelp: Pre-filled with the model that reads best. Change it only if you know why.
saveNeedsTest: Test the key first; Save turns on once it works.
verdictFailedHelp: That is the provider's own message. See "What can go wrong" above.
privacy1: The key is encrypted before it is stored. Nobody at AFC can read it back; this page shows only its last four characters.
privacy2: It is sent to the provider you chose and nowhere else. When the AI engine reads a screenshot, that screenshot goes to your provider.
privacy3: You can revoke the key at the provider any time and paste a new one here. Every connect, test and disconnect is listed below with who did it.
toastLoadFailed: Could not load the key page.
toastSaved: Key saved. OCR now runs on your {provider} account.
toastSaveFailed: The key could not be saved.
toastDisconnectFailed: The key could not be disconnected.

gate.fallback: Could not read that screenshot. Please try again.
gate.freeReadSpent: That was AFC's free read. Connect your own AI key to keep using OCR.

admin.title: OCR keys
admin.description: Which organizations read on their own AI key, what they read, and the free reads AFC still pays for.
admin.afcMonth: AFC's own key this month: {reads} reads, about {usd}.

gemini.freeTier: Yes, with daily limits on an AI Studio key.
steps: Open aistudio.google.com and sign in with any Google account.
Press Get API key in the left menu.
Press Create API key. Choose an existing Google Cloud project or let it create one.
Copy the key. It starts with AIza. Treat it like a password.
Optional but wise: in Google Cloud, restrict this key to the Generative Language API only.

openai.freeTier: No. Pay as you go; add a few dollars of credit under Billing first.
steps: Open platform.openai.com and sign in.
Under Settings, open Billing and add credit (a few dollars lasts a whole season).
Open API keys in the left menu and press Create new secret key.
Name it AFC OCR, choose Restricted and allow only Model capabilities.
Copy the key. It starts with sk-. It is shown once.

anthropic.freeTier: No. Pay as you go; add credit under Plans and billing first.
steps: Open console.anthropic.com and sign in.
Under Plans and billing, add credit.
Open Settings, then API keys, and press Create key.
Name it AFC OCR and choose the workspace it belongs to.
Copy the key. It starts with sk-ant-. It is shown once.

openrouter.freeTier: Some models are free with limits; the recommended one is pay as you go.
steps: Open openrouter.ai and sign in (Google or GitHub works).
Open Credits and add a few dollars.
Open Keys and press Create key.
Name it AFC OCR. A credit limit on the key is a good idea.
Copy the key. It starts with sk-or-.
Open console.groq.com and sign in.
Open API Keys in the left menu and press Create API Key.
Name it AFC OCR.
Copy the key. It starts with gsk_. It is shown once.
Open console.mistral.ai and sign in.
Choose a plan under Billing (the free experiment plan works for OCR).
Open API Keys and press Create new key.
Name it AFC OCR and copy it. It is shown once.
Open console.x.ai and sign in with your X account.
Add credit under Billing.
Open API Keys and press Create API key.
Name it AFC OCR and copy it. It starts with xai-.
Find your provider's OpenAI-compatible base URL (it usually ends in /v1).
Find the id of a model that can read images.
Create a key in your provider's console.
Paste the base URL, the model id and the key below, then Test.
